prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: compositional option two for the approved Cathode Gauze visual system of the native iOS Last Train app
Primary request: Create a high-fidelity portrait iPhone app screen that explores a ROUTE STRIKE composition while keeping the Cathode Gauze identity completely fixed.
Scene/backdrop: full-bleed 393x852-style app screen only, no phone frame and no marketing poster.
Exact visible content: "LAST TRAIN", "FAST TRAIN", "Upminster", "EAST", "23:47", "Shoeburyness", "22:58", "23:18", "23:32", "FIRST BACK", "05:12", "Direct services only".
Product task: reveal the final direct train within two seconds, with earlier departures and first train back subordinate. No durations. No +1 or calendar-next-day labels.
Fixed visual world: deep ink-blue black plane, fine bronze anode gauze, ghosted cathode numerals, bone-white text, warm cathode orange for ordinary active information, #FF304C reserved only for the last train. One condensed numeral-led display voice; crisp native body text. No rounded glass cards, no dashboard tiles, no bottom tab bar, no decorative illustration.
Composition variation: a narrow persistent left-edge rail identifies Upminster and EAST. A vertical chronological strike line runs down the screen like a precise illuminated rail. Ghost versions of all departure times sit behind this line. The final train 23:47 strikes forward at monumental scale in the upper-right third, glowing red, with Shoeburyness directly attached. Earlier times 22:58, 23:18, 23:32 align as smaller orange rail events below. FIRST BACK 05:12 anchors the bottom. Keep LAST TRAIN / FAST TRAIN as a compact top mode control beneath a clean Dynamic Island safe area.
Interaction implication: the selected train should feel like it can snap forward from its ghost state and relay to the Dynamic Island.
Constraints: production-grade native iOS operating screen; immediately scannable; exact copy readable; red nowhere except the 23:47 last-train event; no gradients that reduce contrast; no fake logos, watermark, phone hardware, ticketing, maps, or advertisements.
